chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, and others, from Yunus, regarding

A mother of a child (Umm al-Walad) who has no child of her own, her child died, and her master died without emancipating her. Is it permissible for anyone to marry her? He said: No, she is a slave. It is not permissible for anyone to marry her except by emancipation from the inheritors. So if she has a child, and there is no debt upon the deceased, then she belongs to the child. And when the child owns her, she has been emancipated by the ownership of her child. And if she is shared between partners, she has been emancipated from the share of her child, and she would work (pay) for the remainder of her price.

key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (concubine who bore her master a child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a Umm al-Walad after her master's death if she was not emancipated?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific juristic status of an 'Umm al-Walad' upon her master's death, establishing that she does not automatically become free but remains a slave until her heirs emancipate her. It details the mechanism of emancipation through inheritance, noting that if she has a child, she belongs to that child (or children), and her ownership by them constitutes her freedom, with the heir(s) responsible for paying off the remaining shares of other co-heirs. This ruling highlights the Shia legal distinction between automatic emancipation and the requirement of heir-initiated manumission in this context.
